description: Phishing e-mail taxonomy: the indicator catalogue behind PhishGate's three verdict labels (benign, suspicious, phishing). The label of a mail is decided by the rule in schemas/verdict.py (label_from_reasons, mirrored in docs/labels.md) from the reason codes the model cites; this file never decides a label. Each primary category names its indicators, the reason codes usually present, and the side it belongs to (`label`: benign for legitimate and commercial_spam, phishing for the six attack categories; a mail of an attack category still comes out suspicious when the rule is not met). The analysis prompt lists the categories after the label rule (phishgate/intake/taxonomy.py) and the generated corpus carries the category of every mail (scripts/make_corpus.py, labels.csv column `taxonomy`). Secondary tags describe a mail further; they never change the label. Content indicators are judged by the model only: the verifier keeps checking computed facts and nothing else.
label_source: schemas/verdict.py: label_from_reasons(); same text in docs/labels.md

primary_labels.name: Legitimate
primary_labels.label: benign
primary_labels.definition: Genuine, expected correspondence, including real notifications from services the recipient actually uses.
indicators: content matches a real relationship or transaction

primary_labels.name: Commercial spam
primary_labels.label: benign
primary_labels.definition: Unsolicited bulk marketing with no deception about sender identity or intent. Unwanted but not malicious.
indicators: real brand sending from its own domain

primary_labels.name: Credential phishing (mass/deceptive)
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: Untargeted email impersonating a brand or service to drive the recipient to a fake login or data-entry page.
indicators: password expiry or account suspension theme
package delivery or document share theme
link to a login page on a lookalike or unrelated domain

primary_labels.name: Spear phishing
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: Credential or malware lure visibly personalised to the recipient or their organisation. Includes lateral phishing sent from compromised internal accounts.
indicators: recipient name, role or colleagues referenced
sender appears to be a known contact

primary_labels.name: Business Email Compromise / payment fraud
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: Impersonates an executive, vendor or employee to request a wire transfer, invoice change, payroll or bank-detail update, or gift-card purchase. Typically plain text with no link or attachment.
indicators: request to pay, transfer or change banking details
vendor invoice with new account details

primary_labels.name: Malware delivery
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: Primary objective is to get the recipient to open an attachment or download a file that executes a payload.
indicators: link to a direct file download

primary_labels.name: Advance-fee / consumer scam
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: Promises money, prizes, inheritance, romance or charity in exchange for a reply, fee or personal data. Also covers sextortion and other extortion emails.
indicators: extortion threat with payment demand (often cryptocurrency)

primary_labels.name: Callback / hybrid
primary_labels.label: phishing
primary_labels.definition: No link or attachment; pushes the recipient to phone a number or switch to another channel (SMS, WhatsApp).
indicators: phone number as the only call to action
instruction to contact support to cancel a charge

tie_break_precedence: rules apply in the listed order; the first rule that matches decides the category

tie_break_rules.rule: Targeted email with a link or attachment payload -> spear_phishing. Targeted email requesting money or banking changes with no payload -> bec_payment_fraud.
Link to a login or data-entry page -> credential_phishing. Attachment or download that executes code -> malware_delivery, even if themed as an invoice.
A real notification from a legitimate service (e.g. DocuSign, WeTransfer) that leads to malicious content is labelled by its destination (credential_phishing or malware_delivery), not by its sender.
Personalisation to the recipient or organisation decides spear_phishing versus credential_phishing or malware_delivery, not the brand being impersonated.
A money request with no link and no attachment is bec_payment_fraud when targeted and callback_hybrid when mass-mailed with a phone number as the only call to action.
Unsolicited marketing with no impersonation and no credential or payment request -> commercial_spam, not phishing.

vector.note: an empty list means the mail carries no vector

impersonated_sector.reference: Saka et al. (2024) Phishing Codebook sectors

persuasion.reference: Ferreira, Coventry & Lenzini (2015), with urgency and threat kept separate
